ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is a rectangle in the figure, with four congruent and tangent circles arranged horizontally inside it. Point P is the upper-right vertex of the rectangle; point Q is on the upper side and is the point of tangency of the third circle with the upper side of the rectangle; point R is on the lower side and is the point of tangency of the second circle with the lower side of the rectangle. Segments PQ, PR, and QR form triangle PQR. Reasoning: The radius of each circle is 6 cm, so the height of the rectangle is equal to one diameter, namely 12 cm. The horizontal distance between adjacent centers of circles is also one diameter, namely 12 cm. Q is directly above the third circle, and P is at the vertex of the rectangle to the right of the fourth circle, so the horizontal length of QP is equal to 12 cm from the center of the third circle to the center of the fourth circle, plus 6 cm from the radius of the fourth circle to the right boundary, for a total of 18 cm. Because QP is on the upper side of the rectangle and R is on the lower side of the rectangle, the perpendicular distance from R to line QP is the height of the rectangle, 12 cm. The area of the triangle is (1/2) × 18 × 12 = 108 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/base-height setup. From the image, note that the four equal circles are arranged in one horizontal row inside the rectangle; P is the upper-right rectangle vertex, Q is the top tangency point of the third circle, and R is the bottom tangency point of the second circle. From the text, each circle has radius 6, so the rectangle height is one diameter, 12 cm, and consecutive circle centers/tangency points are separated horizontally by one diameter, 12 cm. Since Q is above the third circle center and P is at the right edge beyond the fourth circle, QP equals one center-to-center gap from the third to fourth circle plus one radius to the right wall: 12 + 6 = 18 cm. The perpendicular distance from R on the bottom side to the top side containing QP is 12 cm. Therefore area of triangle PQR is 1/2 * 18 * 12 = 108 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Use a rectangle-complement area decomposition. From the image, take the auxiliary rectangle whose lower-left corner is R, upper-right corner is P, and whose top side contains Q. The horizontal distance from R to P spans from the second circle’s bottom tangency point to the right side of the rectangle: from circle 2 to circle 3 is 12 cm, circle 3 to circle 4 is 12 cm, and from circle 4 center to the right side is 6 cm, so RP’s horizontal span is 30 cm. Inside it, subtract the right triangle below segment RP, with legs 30 and 12, area 180, and subtract the left top right triangle between R, Q, and the vertical projection of R on the top side, with legs 12 and 12, area 72. The remaining region is triangle PQR, so its area is 360 - 180 - 72 = 108 cm^2.
